shared_elements: low-relief carving on a single stone block/slab
profile animal or creature figures with visible legs
horizontal band of repeated geometric pattern (zigzag/hatching) dividing the field
row of repeated similar motifs in a register
small disc/circular elements within the figural field
irregular upper edge / shaped top of the stone
justification: Both are shallow-relief carvings on a shaped stone monolith in which a field of profile creatures is separated from a further register by a continuous horizontal band of repetitive geometric hatching, with a row of similar repeated motifs running the width of the stone — a genuinely comparable register-and-band scheme. The chief differences are the physical format and the register order: A is a flat rectangular slab with its patterned band and cartouche-like panels at the bottom beneath a crowded scene, whereas B is a three-dimensional pillar with a projecting head-block whose band sits high, and its figures are looser, more naturalistic animals scattered over the surface rather than A's compact, angular, tightly interlocked figures.}
